The comparative clinical outcomes between Direct Oral Anticoagulants ([[doac|DOAC]]) and the traditional vitamin K antagonist [[marevan|Marevan]] are closely monitored to evaluate treatment efficacy and patient safety. A key metric in this evaluation is [[indikator-5|Indikator 5]], which tracks the incidence of ischemic apoplexy (ischemic stroke) among treated patients.

According to the 2024 registry data, the proportion of patients who experienced an ischemic apoplexy was 0.89% for those treated with [[doac|DOAC]], compared to 0.51% for those treated with [[marevan|Marevan]] [^src1]. This comparative result highlights a measurable difference in stroke incidence between the two anticoagulant therapies within the tracked patient population, providing critical data for clinical guidelines and treatment evaluations.

## Claims

**AFDK_2024.pdf, page 49**
- Andelen af patienter med iskæmisk apopleksi er 0,89% for DOAC og 0,51% for marevan [^src1] (doac, marevan, indikator-5)
